podcast.title: Future Potential
podcast.body: It is suggested that if he can navigate the public criticism often directed at Nickelback, he has the potential to become as prominent, or even more so, than his Canadian superproducer predecessors. "So you watch if he can survive the Nickelback wine he could end up as big or bigger than some of his Canadian super producer predecessors."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Nickelback Success
podcast.body: Chad Kroeger is a member of Nickelback, a band that has sold over 10 million albums. "Nickelback has sold more than 10 million albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Potential for Self-Plagiarism Defense
podcast.body: Chad Kroeger is envisioned as potentially needing to defend himself in a similar way to John Fogarty if ever accused of self-plagiarism, due to Nickelback's consistent songwriting formula. "However, should Chief Nickelback, Dude Chad Kruger ever find himself in the same situation as John Fogarty, he'd probably have to defend himself in much the same way."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Residency
podcast.body: Chad Kroeger has chosen to remain in Canada. "Some like Chad and Greg and Arnold have elected to remain in Canada."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rising Industry Mogul
podcast.body: In a relatively short period, Chad Kroeger has become one of the most powerful and sought-after figures in music. With his own Vancouver-based record label, 604 Records, and Nickelback's private recording studio, he is positioned as an industry mogul. "and now that he has his own record label the Vancouver based 604 records and now that Nickelback has their own recording studio Chad has set up to be some kind of industry mogul."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Chad Kroeger's Work Style
xref.body: Ian Thorneley respects Chad Kroeger's brilliance but notes that Kroeger's successful working style differs from his own. This difference sometimes led to external pressure from others trying to impose Kroeger's methods on Ian's projects. "But the way that he works is very different than the way that I work."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ian Thornley - In His Own Words: Part 2

xref.title: Connection with Chad Kroeger
xref.body: Ian Thorneley has worked extensively with Chad Kroeger of Nickelback, considering him a close friend and family member. However, he acknowledges that Kroeger's successful working methods differ significantly from his own, leading to external pressures from those trying to replicate Kroeger's success. "But having said that, he, he, I, that I've worked a lot with the guy and he's like, he's like a family member and he's a very close guy and very close friend."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Public Perception
xref.body: The band faces public criticism, referred to as "the Nickelback wine," which Chad Kroeger is seen as needing to "survive" to reach his full potential as a producer. "So you watch if he can survive the Nickelback wine he could end up as big or bigger than some of his Canadian super producer predecessors."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
